title: First Light over Nairobi

best_window.label: 8:00 AM–11:00 AM
best_window.reason: The strongest outdoor window: dry, calm, with 14% average rain probability.

city_context.brief: Nairobi, is the capital and largest city of Kenya, located in the south-central part of the country. As of 2026, it has a population of 5.6 million and a metropolitan population of 15.95 million, making it the 8th most populous city in Africa and the 4th most populous metropolitan area. The city goes beyond its borders and has expanded into neighbouring counties, making it the 4th largest metropolitan area in Africa.
city_context.fact: The name Nairobi comes from the Maasai phrase Enkare Nairobi, commonly translated as “place of cool waters.”

poem: Above Nairobi, warm light gathers at the roofs,
the wind carries one color into another,
and morning begins before anyone asks it to.

title: First Light over Kyoto

best_window.label: 3–6 PM
best_window.reason: A mild, mostly dry three-hour stretch with manageable wind.

city_context.brief: Kyoto was Japan's imperial capital for more than a millennium. Its grid, temples, gardens, craft traditions, and layered neighborhoods still carry that history into daily life.
city_context.fact: Kyoto served as Japan's imperial capital from 794 until the imperial court moved to Tokyo in 1869.

poem: Above Kyoto, pale light crosses the open sky,
the wind carries one color into another,
and morning begins before anyone asks it to.

title: First Light over Reykjavik

best_window.label: 3–6 PM
best_window.reason: A mild, mostly dry three-hour stretch with manageable wind.

city_context.brief: Reykjavík is Iceland's capital and largest city, set on Faxaflói bay amid a landscape shaped by glaciers, geothermal heat, and the North Atlantic.
city_context.fact: Reykjavík is the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state.

poem: Above Reykjavik, pale light crosses the open sky,
the wind carries one color into another,
and morning begins before anyone asks it to.
